memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: ""Therefore, say to the Israelites: 'I am the Lord, and I will bring you out from under the yoke of the Egyptians. I will free you from being slaves to them, and I will redeem you with an outstretched arm and with mighty acts of judgment.'"" - Exodus 6:6 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Count the "I wills" in this verse. I will bring you out. I will free you. I will redeem you. Salvation, from start to finish, is God's initiative.

Israel contributed nothing to their rescue. They did not organise a revolt or negotiate their release. They groaned, and God acted.

Look particularly at the word redeem. In Israel's world, a redeemer was a family member who paid the price to buy back a relative who had fallen into slavery or lost their land. It was not charity from a stranger. It was a kinsman spending his own resources for his own family.

That word runs like a golden thread through Scripture until it reaches the cross. Christ did not redeem us with silver or gold, but with His own precious blood (1 Pet 1:18-19). He became our kinsman — taking on flesh — so that He could pay what we could never pay.

If you feel unable to free yourself from something today, that is exactly the condition redemption addresses.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Am I still trying to earn what God has already accomplished for me?
2. What does it mean to me today that Jesus paid the price to buy me back?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord Jesus, thank You for becoming my Redeemer and paying a price I could never afford. I rest in Your finished work. Amen.
